content.text:
Should You Buy Intel Stock as Its Foundry Turnaround Takes Shape?: The search result identifies the article, author, and Oct. 3 publication time. The page’s revision history or a pre-cutoff snapshot was not independently verified; the supplied AOL copy carries the full text and a pre-cutoff timestamp. (time=2026-10-03 14:45 EST (as labeled on page; UTC offset uncertain); cutoff=UNKNOWN).
Intel (INTC) Q2 2026 Earnings Call Transcript & Audio: The transcript renders CEO Lip-Bu Tan’s remarks on 14A customer engagement, the PDK 0.9 milestone, and customers considering products and capacity as they see the PDK and yield. It also records CFO David Zinsner discussing capacity investment across internal and external demand. It is a transcript, not Intel’s official written disclosure. (time=UNKNOWN; cutoff=UNKNOWN).
Intel Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 27, 2026: Reports Q2 Foundry revenue of $5.765 billion, including $5.5 billion intersegment revenue and $293 million external revenue; the filing says the external-revenue increase was primarily due to Altera’s transition to an external customer. Foundry operating loss was $2.089 billion, and the filing says substantially all Foundry business supported Intel’s internal manufacturing. (time=2026-07-24; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
Intel Reports Second-Quarter 2026 Financial Results: Intel’s July 23 release reports Q2 revenue of $16.1 billion, up 25% year over year, and announces the public earnings call. The fuller Foundry revenue breakdown is in the 10-Q. (time=2026-07-23; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
Intel says it has two prospective customers for 14A — expects to hear about commitments in second half of 2026: Reports that two prospective customers were exploring 14A test chips, but Intel then had no committed external 14A customers. It said firm supplier decisions were expected from the second half of 2026 into the first half of 2027, with capacity investment tied to customer commitments. (time=2026-01-23; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
